QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_4

question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (Cat III, close-ended, 5-year tenor) has committed capital of INR 80 crore. At end of Year 5, NAV (pre-incentives) is INR 110 crore. Hurdle rate is 10% (simple annual). Reference Hurdle NAV = 80 x (1.10)^5 = INR 128.84 crore. Incentive fee rate is 20%. What incentive fee is payable to the manager?

answer.text: Zero — NAV is below Reference Hurdle

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Amount for incentive = max(0, NAV − higher of HWM and Reference Hurdle). NAV = 110 cr < Reference Hurdle 128.84 cr → amount = 0 → incentive fee = 0. The manager earns zero carry despite the fund being up INR 30 cr, because the hurdle was not cleared. **The Trap:** INR 6 cr treats 20% of 30 cr gain without the hurdle test. INR 4 cr treats 20% of (110 − 80 − 20 set-aside). INR 22 cr is absurd but tempts as 20% of 110. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D Cat I/II Manager would also use hurdle, but with a catch-up tier common in PE. Cat III on XIX-E rarely has catch-up; straight HWM/Hurdle logic is tested. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In underperforming years, investors sometimes pressure managers to redeem at HWM to reset the carry ratchet. Your LPA should explicitly lock the HWM to the UNIT SERIES, not a redeeming LP, else the next LP gets an unfair free option.
